questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street going the wrong way.
You can go if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street going the wrong way.
questions.explanation: If you pass these signs, you are going the wrong way. You risk a head-on collision. Turn around safely.

questions.question: You are in an accident and your car is blocking traffic. You should:

options.text: Move your vehicle out of the roadway if you can.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the roadway if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle out of the roadway if you can. Do not leave the scene without giving your information and helping if needed.

questions.question: Your body removes about how much alcohol per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One drink an hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body removes about one drink per hour. However, how impaired you get depends on many things: how much you drink, how fast you drink, your weight, whether you've eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you has broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do it safely without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you:

options.text: Can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
Cannot turn and must go straight.
Still have the right to turn.
Do not have to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the arrow's direction. But you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A solid white line in the middle of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic goes opposite ways and passing is not allowed.
Traffic goes opposite ways and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic goes the same way and passing is not allowed.
Traffic goes the same way and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic goes the same way and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When two cars enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, which car must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, when two cars arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to return to the main road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the bus.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus signaling to pull back onto the road after stopping. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: You can cross double solid yellow lines:
questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you use?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.
The lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down after you enter the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you enter the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until after you enter the exit ramp.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers will let you through.
Drive around a car if it blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another vehicle hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive faster than the speed limit while passing another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You cannot exceed the posted speed limit at any time, even when passing another vehicle.

questions.question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?
questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and can reduce your visibility.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: What effect does drinking coffee have after drinking alcohol?

options.text: It eliminates the effects of alcohol.
It has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not reduce your blood alcohol concentration. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a factor in how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system pushes fumes out of your vehicle and keeps them out of the passenger area. A leaky exhaust system lets dangerous carbon monoxide into your car. Fix any leaks right away.

questions.question: Under normal driving conditions, you should stay at least this far behind the car ahead:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Use the three-second rule to stay a safe distance from the car in front of you. This rule works for regular-size vehicles driving under normal conditions.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to go after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, look for a train on the other track before going.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, look for a train on the other track before going.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming on either track.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal only as you move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet ahead when on residential streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Cars and motorcycles can hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before turning or changing lanes on a residential street. On a freeway, signal five seconds before changing lanes.

questions.question: Drivers should watch closely for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes with motorcycles, bikes, and pedestrians happen because drivers did not see them. These are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They may move faster and have dim lights. Stay alert for these smaller, more vulnerable road users.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways at the intersection.
Always come to a full stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. It tells you to slow down and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, let pedestrians and oncoming vehicles go first.

questions.question: If you see both a red light and a green arrow, you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow until the red light changes.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You can turn in the direction of a green arrow after you yield to other traffic in the intersection or crosswalk, even if a red light is showing.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left since the road is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely. After you stop, you can go when the way is clear.

questions.question: Regular roads freeze before ramps and bridges.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Ramps and bridges are in the air, so they freeze faster than regular roads in cold weather. Drive slowly and carefully when crossing bridges in freezing temperatures.
